newsitem.title: USA: Bill planned to make stable prices Fed's main goal.
newsitem.headline: Bill planned to make stable prices Fed's main goal.

text.p: A key House Republican lawmaker said on Monday he planned to introduce new legislation soon to mandate price stability as the Federal Reserve's primary goal.

"Price stability is important since it provides the essential foundation for sustainable long-run economic and employment growth," Jim Saxton, Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee (JEC) of Congress, said in a statement.
Under the Humphrey-Hawkins Act, the central bank is required to seek balanced economic growth with maximum employment and price stability.

Earlier this year, Saxton, from New Jersey, and Republican Senator Connie Mack from Florida introduced legislation that would abolish the Humphrey-Hawkins Act and make price stability the central focus of the Fed.
JEC economist Bob Keleher said the new legislation would not seek to abolish the Humphery-Hawkins Act.
Instead, it would allow the Fed to pursue other economic goals as long as they did not conflict with its primary long-term objective of price stability.
"It allows for a gradualist approach to achieving price stability which is less disruptive to the economy," he said.

That could help win support for the bill from lawmakers who in the past have shied away from making price stability the Fed's sole mandate out of fear that single-minded pursuit of that goal could hurt the economy.
Under the Saxton bill, which will be introduced in weeks, the Fed would be required to set numerical goals for price stability and a timetable for achieving that, Keleher said.
